breakfast.name: Mangú (Mashed Plantains)
instructions: Peel green plantains, cut into chunks, boil in salted water until very tender — 20 min
Drain, reserving some cooking water
Mash plantains with butter, adding cooking water for smoothness — it should be creamy, not gluey
Make los tres golpes (the three hits) to go with it:
Fry salami until crispy on both sides
Fry eggs sunny-side up
Pickle onions: sauté sliced red onion in oil with vinegar until soft and tangy
Plate mangú topped with pickled onion, fried salami, and fried egg alongside
Some add fried cheese for the fourth 'hit'
breakfast.description: Mashed green plantain with 'los tres golpes' (the three hits): fried salami, fried egg, and pickled red onion. THE Dominican breakfast — eaten every single morning by millions. The pickled onion on top is non-negotiable.

breakfast.name: Avena (Oat Drink)
instructions: Cook oats in milk with cinnamon and lime zest
Add sugar and vanilla
Blend until smooth
Serve warm or cold
breakfast.description: Creamy oat beverage with cinnamon and lime.

breakfast.name: Yaroa (Dominican Loaded Fries)
instructions: Fry thick-cut potatoes until golden and crispy
Cook seasoned meat (ground beef with sofrito)
Layer in a takeaway container: fries on bottom, meat on top
Drizzle heavily with ketchup and mayonnaise
Cover with mozzarella cheese
Put under broiler until cheese melts
Eat with a fork — it's a beautiful mess
breakfast.description: Loaded fries — a late-night Dominican street creation. Fries buried under seasoned meat, ketchup, mayo, and melted cheese. Eaten at 2am from a food cart after a night out.

breakfast.name: Mangú con Los Tres Golpes
ingredients: Los tres golpes: fried eggs, fried Dominican salami, fried white cheese
Pickled red onions (cebolla curtida): red onion, lime juice, vinegar, oregano, olive oil
instructions: Boil plantains until very tender
Mash with butter, cooking water, and a splash of milk — must be smooth but thick
The key: add cold water to hot plantain while mashing — this is the Dominican technique for silky texture
Fry eggs sunny-side up
Fry sliced Dominican salami until crispy and curled
Fry thick slices of queso blanco until golden
Make cebolla curtida: slice red onion, soak in lime juice and vinegar with oregano and olive oil
Plate mangú in center, arrange the three strikes around it: eggs, salami, cheese
Top mangú with pickled onions
This is THE Dominican breakfast — 'los tres golpes' means 'the three strikes'
breakfast.description: The Dominican Republic's national breakfast — mashed green plantain with 'the three strikes': fried egg, fried salami, and fried cheese, topped with tangy pickled red onions. Mangú videos showing the cold-water mashing technique are viral Dominican food content, and the dish is a point of fierce national pride.

lunch.name: La Bandera (The Flag)
ingredients: White rice (2 cups, cooked fluffy — each grain separate)
Red kidney beans: cooked with sofrito (onion, garlic, pepper, cilantro, oregano), tomato sauce, cumin
Carne guisada (stewed chicken or beef): seasoned with sazón, adobo, oregano, braised in tomato
instructions: Cook rice: rinse until water runs clear, cook with oil and salt — every grain must be separate, never sticky
Make beans: sauté sofrito (onion, garlic, pepper, cilantro), add cooked beans, tomato sauce, cumin, simmer until thick and creamy
Make meat: season chicken or beef with sazón, adobo, oregano, brown, then braise in tomato sauce until tender
Fry tostones or sweet plantain
Plate: rice takes half the plate, beans go over the rice, meat alongside, salad on the side, plantain on the edge
The rice must be white and fluffy — Dominican identity is partly rice identity
lunch.description: The Flag — rice, beans, and meat, the daily lunch of every Dominican. Named because the red beans, white rice, and meat represent the flag's colors. It is eaten so universally that 'lunch' and 'la bandera' are practically synonyms.

lunch.name: Sancocho (Seven-Meat Stew)
instructions: In a massive pot, brown seasoned meat pieces (traditionally seven meats: chicken, pork, goat, beef, longaniza, smoked pork, beef ribs)
Add water, bring to simmer
Add root vegetables in order of cooking time: yuca and yam first, then potato, then green plantain, then corn
Add sofrito: sautéed onion, garlic, pepper, cilantro, recao (culantro)
Add sour orange juice or lime juice — the acid is essential
Simmer until everything is tender and broth is thick from the dissolved starches
The broth should be cloudy and substantial — not a clear soup
Serve in large bowls with white rice on the side and avocado
Made for Christmas, New Year's, or whenever the whole family gathers
lunch.description: Seven-meat stew with root vegetables — the Dominican gathering dish. Making sancocho is a family event: everyone helps, everyone eats. The broth is thick, the meats varied, and the bowl is bottomless. A national ritual more than a recipe.

lunch.name: Chivo Guisado (Stewed Goat)
ingredients: Sour orange juice (or lime + orange juice)
instructions: Marinate goat in sour orange, garlic, oregano, sazón for 2+ hours
Brown goat pieces in oil
Add onion, pepper, garlic, cook until soft
Add tomato paste, wine, olives, capers
Add water to partially cover
Braise low and slow, 90 min, until goat is fall-off-bone tender
The sauce should reduce to thick, dark gravy
Serve with white rice and tostones
lunch.description: Slow-braised goat — the sour orange marinade tenderizes the meat and adds a citrus depth. A weekend and celebration dish, especially in the Cibao region.

dinner.name: Mofongo
ingredients: Garlic (6+ cloves, mashed into paste with olive oil and salt)
Broth: chicken or shrimp broth to pour over
instructions: Peel plantains, slice into thick rounds
Fry in oil until golden but not too crispy — they'll be mashed
While hot, place fried plantain in a pilón (wooden mortar)
Add mashed garlic-oil paste and crushed chicharrón
Pound with pestle — the motion is fold and press, not smash
The mofongo should be chunky-smooth, not puréed — texture matters
Shape into a dome in a bowl
Pour hot chicken or shrimp broth around the base
Serve with stewed shrimp, chicken, or pork on top
dinner.description: Fried plantain mashed with garlic and pork cracklings in a wooden mortar — Puerto Rican in origin but deeply Dominican. The pilón pounding is rhythmic and practiced. Served in a dome with broth pooling around it.

dinner.name: Pescado con Coco (Fish in Coconut)
instructions: Season fish with lime and salt
Sauté vegetables
Add coconut milk, simmer
Add fish, cook gently 15 min
Garnish with cilantro

dinner.name: Pollo al Horno Dominicano (Dominican Baked Chicken)
ingredients: Marinade: sour orange juice, garlic, oregano, sazón, adobo, cumin, black pepper, olive oil
instructions: Season chicken aggressively with all spices and sour orange — really rub it in
Marinate overnight if possible — at minimum 2 hours
Place in roasting pan with onion, pepper, potatoes
Roast at 190°C for 55-60 min, basting with pan juices
The skin should be golden, crispy, and deeply seasoned
The adobo and sazón create a flavor profile that is distinctly Dominican
Serve with rice, beans, and ensalada verde
dinner.description: Dominican roast chicken — what makes it Dominican is the aggressive seasoning: sazón, adobo, sour orange, and oregano. Every Dominican can identify this chicken by smell alone.

snacks.name: Empanadas de Yuca
ingredients: Dough: 1kg yuca (cassava, boiled and mashed), 2 tbsp butter, salt, achiote oil (for color)
Filling: seasoned ground beef with sofrito, olives, capers, hard-boiled egg
Ketchup to serve (yes, ketchup — this is Dominican tradition)
instructions: Boil yuca until very soft, drain, mash until completely smooth — no lumps or they'll crack when frying
Mix with butter, salt, and achiote oil for golden color
Flatten a ball of dough in your palm
Place filling in center: seasoned beef, a piece of olive, a slice of hard-boiled egg
Close and seal edges — the yuca dough is more fragile than wheat, handle gently
Deep fry until golden and crispy — the yuca shell should shatter when bitten
Serve with ketchup — this is the authentic Dominican way
snacks.description: Crispy yuca-dough empanadas — the cassava shell shatters into crispy shards when you bite through to the seasoned beef filling. Served with ketchup, which foreigners question and Dominicans defend fiercely.

snacks.name: Chimichurri Burger (Dominican Street Burger)
ingredients: Cabbage slaw (shredded cabbage, tomato, onion, lime)
instructions: Season patties with sazón, garlic, oregano
Grill or fry until cooked through
Toast the pan de agua bun
Layer: bun, ketchup, mayo, patty, cabbage slaw
Smash it all together
Serve with fries or tostones on the side
snacks.description: Not to be confused with Argentine chimichurri sauce — this is the Dominican street burger. Loaded with cabbage slaw and sauces in a soft pan de agua bun. The late-night fuel of Santo Domingo.

desserts.name: Habichuelas con Dulce
ingredients: 2 cups red kidney beans (cooked very soft)
Whole milk cookies (galletas de leche) to serve
instructions: Blend cooked beans until very smooth
Strain through a fine sieve — the dessert must be silky, no bean skins
Heat bean purée with evaporated milk, coconut milk, cinnamon, cloves
Add diced sweet potato, cook until tender
Add sugar, butter, raisins, vanilla
Simmer until thick and creamy — it should coat a spoon
Chill — it's served cold during Lent and Easter
Pour into glasses or bowls, top with milk cookies for dipping
The cookies get soft as they soak up the bean cream
desserts.description: Sweet bean cream — a Lenten dessert of puréed red beans with coconut milk, spices, and sweet potato. Sounds impossible, tastes like a rich, creamy pudding. Served cold during Holy Week to the whole neighborhood. Dominicans bring it door to door.

desserts.name: Bizcocho Dominicano (Dominican Cake)
ingredients: Cake: butter, sugar, eggs, flour, baking powder, milk, vanilla, pineapple juice
Meringue frosting: egg whites, sugar, cream of tartar
Pineapple filling: crushed pineapple, sugar, cornstarch
instructions: Cream butter and sugar, add eggs one at a time
Add flour alternately with milk and pineapple juice
Bake in layers at 175°C for 25-30 min
Make pineapple filling: cook crushed pineapple with sugar and cornstarch until thick
Make meringue: whip egg whites with sugar and cream of tartar until stiff and glossy
Assemble: cake layer, pineapple filling, repeat, frost with meringue
The meringue should be dramatically swirled and tall
Torch or broil meringue peaks until golden
desserts.description: The Dominican birthday cake — yellow cake with pineapple filling and dramatic meringue frosting. Every birthday, every quinceañera, every celebration. The meringue is piled sky-high.

drinks.name: Morir Soñando (To Die Dreaming)
instructions: Mix cold milk with sugar and vanilla
Slowly add cold orange juice while stirring
Serve immediately over ice
drinks.description: Creamy orange-milk drink — do not let it curdle.

drinks.name: Mamajuana
ingredients: Bark and herbs: cat's claw bark, timacle bark, bohuco root, star anise, cinnamon sticks, cloves (pre-packaged mamajuana bark mix)
instructions: Fill bottle with bark and herbs — these are sold as pre-packaged mixes across the DR
First soak: fill with cheap red wine, let sit 1-2 days, then discard the wine (this 'cures' the bark)
Second fill: add equal parts dark rum, red wine, and honey
Let infuse for at least a week — longer is better
Strain and drink in small glasses
The same bark can be re-used for years — just top off with more rum, wine, and honey
Each family's bottle tastes different and is never empty for long
drinks.description: Dominican herbal liqueur — rum, red wine, and honey infused with bark and roots. Every Dominican household has a bottle, constantly refilled. Believed to be an aphrodisiac and general cure-all. The bark lasts for years.
